Finale application installations for macOS and Windows, Finale 1.0.0 through Finale 2011, rather than authored documents; deliverables in research/corpora/rpatters1-installs/. 4536 distinct source hashes across 12116 loose files, so this corpus is heavily duplicated across versions. Surveyed with --sniff-content, without which the classic Mac eras would be invisible: those documents kept the file type in the resource fork and carry no extension. corpus_fingerprint covers loose files only. This corpus now has exports and the semantic half of the pipeline runs: 3090 adjacent-exact companions, being 3066 Finale 2011 documents and the 24 WinFin 2.2 tutorial files. Its companion convention is a '-finale27' directory holding '<stem>.musx', which is NOT the '-exports'/'.fin27.musx' convention rpatters1-main uses. Re-surveyed 2026-08-12 after the Finale 2011 install DVD was imaged and its Mac and Windows payloads mined (count rose from 9764 to 12116). Finale 2011 is version 16.0.0.30, previously unverified in VERSION_MATRIX.md. Excluded: 'Finale PDK' (MakeMusic proprietary, outside this project's provenance boundary); '*.lib', '*.fan' and '*.fpa'; the Finale 2014.5/25/26/27 application bundles (MUSX-era only); and '*/Libraries*', which holds Finale's setting libraries rather than scores and contributed ~900 specimens no era framing classifies. KEEP='*Default*' re-admits the stock font-default files that live inside that excluded tree; the pattern is not '*Font Default*' because 'Handwritten Default' and 'Default Fonts' carry no such substring. Those files still classify under no epoch and recover nothing, which is a reader gap and the reason to keep them visible. inventory.py no longer falls back to a corpus-wide basename search: in a corpus of repeated installs the same filename recurs in every version directory by design, and the previous run's 7266 fallback-ambiguous and 112 fallback-unique pairings were all false, every one of them matching some other version's source to a Finale 2011 export.

Controlled fixtures committed to this repository, surveyed as a corpus in their own right; deliverables in research/corpora/tracked-evidence/. 84 loose *.mus files, all 84 distinct by content and all 84 paired adjacent-exact with a Finale 27 companion, which is the highest companion coverage of any survey and the reason this cohort exists. Its unique contribution is the earliest era: both private corpora begin at Finale 1.8.7, so the only companion-backed Finale 1.0.0 evidence in any survey is the 21 fixtures here, along with the controlled one-variable edit pairs that no authored corpus can supply. Products present: 1.0.0 (21), 2.6 (5), 3.7 (8), 97 (5), 2000 (3), 2002 (3), 2003 (2), 2004b (4), 2005 (11), 2006 (6), 2007 (1), 2008 (1), 2011 (6), 2012 (8). Its companion convention is a '-finale27' directory holding '<stem>.musx', matching rpatters1-installs rather than rpatters1-main. Surveyed without --sniff-content and without archives: every source is named *.mus and committed loose. Unlike the other two surveys the corpus itself ships with the repository, so this row can be re-derived from a clone: run scripts/inventory.py against tests/evidence with the export convention above, which needs no private configuration. The conf that lets ./regenerate.sh drive it alongside the other two lives under the ignored private/ tree like theirs, and holds nothing private. It is tiny by design, so it settles questions about specific eras and must never be read as a percentage. Re-surveyed 2026-08-17 after twelve controlled lyric-options saves were added and the count rose from 69 to 81. The two Finale 2011 fixtures matter out of proportion to their number: **no other survey contains an authored Finale 2011 document at all**, and that release turned out to be where this class's edge-punctuation boundary falls. The installs corpus has 597 companion-backed Finale 2011 documents but they are Finale's own shipped sample content, converted into the release rather than created in it, so they do not show what a new document of that release writes. Several are the only specimen of something: F100-wext-push-6-lift-5.mus names the only two lyric values a Coda-banner document stores; F372-lyricopts-changed.mus is the only document anywhere that varies the hyphen separation; F2000-lyropts-align-just.mus is the only one in any survey that uses the legacy alignment value 3; and the three Finale 2011 auto-numbering saves are the only documents that carry those four fields set at all. F2012-lyric-punct.mus is the only specimen in any survey that carries a lyric punctuation ignore list: Finale writes the list as a variable-length tail on selector 57 and only when it differs from the stock set, so all 1,189 companion-backed documents of the reference corpus are silent on it and no corpus of any size could have located it. F2012-lyropts-noign-punct.mus is the only published document anywhere with the syllable edge-punctuation switch cleared, so it is the sole fixture exercising selector 57 word 4 set rather than clear. Re-surveyed 2026-08-18 after F2006-text-inserts.mus was added and the count rose from 81 to 82. That fixture is the only document in any survey that exercises Finale's text inserts deliberately, and it is the only one that can: Finale 2006 is the first release to write Enigma commands in the binary form and the last to export ETF, so it is the sole version where the same text block exists both encoded and spelled out. Its .mus, .etf and Finale 27 companion agree on all 21 records and together fix 25 of the binary command codes, the full 0-15 digit range, and the fact that an argument is a signed two's-complement value. It also settles that Finale 2006's File Info still has only four fields, so lyricist, arranger and subtitle arrived later. Re-surveyed again the same day after F2008-BE-text-inserts.mus was added and the count rose from 82 to 83. It is the only big-endian Finale 2008 document in any survey, PowerPC-authored because the Intel-era save crashed, and the only one anywhere that carries all seven File Info fields: by that release they have left the header for the text pool. It also carries the four inserts appended past the alphabetical run of command codes and the only one-digit argument, so between it and F2006-text-inserts.mus the two fixtures fix 30 of the codes and all three argument widths. Re-surveyed once more the same day after F2011-text-inserts.mus was added and the count rose from 83 to 84. It closes the binary Enigma command table: Finale 2009 introduced marking categories and Finale 2010 automatic rehearsal marks, so Finale 2011 is the earliest available release able to write ^fontTxt, ^fontMus, ^fontNum and ^rehearsal in one document, and with those four every command musxdom's EnigmaString.h documents has a located code. It also refuted the second and last prediction drawn from the shape of that table: the font-category commands are appended past the inserts at 0xa4-0xa6, not placed among the style commands at 0x80-0x83 where they would belong. Between it, F2006-text-inserts.mus and F2008-BE-text-inserts.mus, no fixture in this corpus reports a command code this reader cannot read.
